11.resolved: Egaˊč = E, g, a, U+02CA MODIFIER LETTER ACUTE ACCENT (stress, postposed to the stressed vowel per keying_spec.md §2.1), č = c + U+030C COMBINING CARON
11.note: mz/ocr/ misread this river name as "Egafé"; raster (zoom 4x, --only 11@60-90) shows Ega + raised stress mark + č clearly. proposal check flagged the bare 'g' as rare (keying_spec.md §5.1, ~93.9% of corpus g's are dotted); contrasted at 4x against the plain English 'g' in "underground" (line 6, --only 6@15-40) — same open loop, same clean white space below the baseline, no dot on either — read as bare g, not g̣.

12.text: Pavlutzky, after some temporary success, was likewise defeated and killed

13.text: March 21, 1747, on the banks of Mayor’s Lake, not far from Markova, on

14.text: the Middle Anadyr. After that, the government, tired of an expensive and

15.text: useless war, withdrew its garrisons, and in 1764 even ordered the fort of

16.text: Anadyrsk, the remotest Russian post in northeastern Asia, to be demolished.

17.text: Intercourse with the Chukchee, renewed in 1789, was carried on the

18.text: whole time with much circumspection, and no new attempt was made to

19.text: conquer the Chukchee by force. The border divisions of the tribe have

20.text: gradually submitted to Russian influence. The bulk of the Chukchee territory,

21.text: however, up to the present time, remains practically exempt from any trace
21.note: A small round speck sits above the 'e' of "exempt" (zoom 4x, --only 21@50-75) — a dot, not a tapered mark, unlike any catalogued diacritic (keying_spec.md §5.9 class: shape at magnification cannot by itself license an uncatalogued codepoint). Read as page dirt, keyed plain "exempt".

22.text: of Russianization; and there are many camps and villages where a Russian

23.text: face has never been seen, nor a word of the Russian language heard.

24.text: About a century ago the territory of the Reindeer Chukchee extended

25.text: beyond the limits of the so-called “Chukchee territory,”¹ — on the Arctic
25.resolved: “ = U+201C LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK, ” = U+201D RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK (curly throughout, keying_spec.md §1/§5.6: "the book sets them throughout and never straight ones"), ¹ = U+00B9 SUPERSCRIPT ONE (footnote marker, keying_spec.md §2.10), — = U+2014 EM DASH (keying_spec.md §2.11)
25.note: mz/ocr/ read the closing quote as a straight \" and the footnote superscript as "!"; raster (zoom 4x, --only 25@57-90) shows curly closing quote and superscript 1 clearly, pairs with the opener on line 42.

26.text: side as far as the river Baranikha, and on the Pacific side to the river Opuka;

27.text: but in the early twenties of the nineteenth century the Reindeer Chukchee,

28.text: induced in a measure by the increase of their herds, began to extend their

29.text: boundaries westward and southward. In the sixties they crossed the Kolyma

30.text: River, and spread over the flat tundra between the Kolyma and the Alaseya;

31.text: the people of some camps even crossed the Alaseya, and went as far as the

32.text: Indighirka. At the same time, other bands went from the Dry Anui to the

33.text: Large Anui, and thence to the Oloi and the Omolon, driving the original

34.text: inhabitants, the Lamut, farther and farther into the woods, or settling side by

35.text: side with them on the borders of the forest.

36.text: On the Pacific side, Chukchee herdsmen rapidly spread beyond their

37.text: former boundaries, and occupied the lower parts of the rivers Opuka, Poqaˊč
37.resolved: Poqaˊč = P, o, q, a, U+02CA MODIFIER LETTER ACUTE ACCENT (stress, postposed), č = c + U+030C COMBINING CARON
37.note: mz/ocr/ read this toponym as "Poga/é"; raster (zoom 4x, --only 37@60-100) shows Poqaˊč clearly, matching the Cyrillic gloss "(Похача)" opening line 38.
